review.intent: Implement G3-owned U1–U8 shared collection instructions and bounded provider history using one new collection_jobs table. Keep physical names, existing metric semantics and external X runtime ownership. Deliver an open PR with CI decided; no collection activation or deployment.

findings.title: Resumed GitHub history trusts a stale public flag
findings.suggested_fix: Always recheck the current reviewed repository identity and public visibility before unfinished history requests. Treat a now-private repo as inaccessible.
findings.first_evidence: A one-request interrupted run caches repository metadata. On resume the transport counterexample changes private to true; the collector reaches the content endpoint without another repository visibility request.
findings.why_it_matters: Resumed GitHub history trusts a stale public flag
findings.evidence: A one-request interrupted run caches repository metadata. On resume the transport counterexample changes private to true; the collector reaches the content endpoint without another repository visibility request.
findings.validation_reason: Source inspection plus failing regression; module size directly measured.

findings.title: Sorted aliases choose the wrong current GitHub name
findings.suggested_fix: Record current_full_name separately from the alias set during review and use that label, with the original reviewed snapshot as the legacy fallback.
findings.first_evidence: Reviewing publisher/family then publisher/aaa leaves sorted aliases with family last. The transport returns 404 for the old name and the expected release evidence is absent.
findings.why_it_matters: Sorted aliases choose the wrong current GitHub name
findings.evidence: Reviewing publisher/family then publisher/aaa leaves sorted aliases with family last. The transport returns 404 for the old name and the expected release evidence is absent.
findings.validation_reason: Source inspection plus failing regression; module size directly measured.

findings.title: Google exclusion misses linked company aliases
findings.suggested_fix: Reject requested brands whose existing BrandCompany relation names Google, as well as a literal google brand.
findings.first_evidence: The Google company-alias regression links one of the twenty-one requested brands to Google; cohort construction currently succeeds instead of raising.
findings.why_it_matters: Google exclusion misses linked company aliases
findings.evidence: The Google company-alias regression links one of the twenty-one requested brands to Google; cohort construction currently succeeds instead of raising.
findings.validation_reason: Source inspection plus failing regression; module size directly measured.

findings.title: Malformed HF history continuation is reported as complete
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror list_page: a Link header mentioning next that cannot be parsed into a valid cursor returns invalid_continuation.
findings.first_evidence: A malformed Link rel=next counterexample currently returns ok with no continuation.
findings.why_it_matters: Malformed HF history continuation is reported as complete
findings.evidence: A malformed Link rel=next counterexample currently returns ok with no continuation.
findings.validation_reason: Source inspection plus failing regression; module size directly measured.

findings.title: New historical orchestration module crosses 1,000 lines
findings.suggested_fix: Move native evidence, sparse archive admission, publication acquisition and cohort interval validation into focused modules while retaining existing public imports.
findings.first_evidence: The newly introduced module contains 1,206 lines combining four independently testable responsibilities; the maintainability rubric flags new files above 1,000 lines.
findings.why_it_matters: New historical orchestration module crosses 1,000 lines
findings.evidence: The newly introduced module contains 1,206 lines combining four independently testable responsibilities; the maintainability rubric flags new files above 1,000 lines.

findings.title: CI does not run the new shared collection regression tests
findings.suggested_fix: Add new collection/provider/cohort paths and test files to the existing PostgreSQL regression workflow; preserve its legacy coverage.
findings.first_evidence: The workflow test command selects existing benchmark/HF tests but none of the new test_collection*, GitHub client/catalog, cohort/inventory/history tests.
findings.why_it_matters: A future broken shared claim, mapping or history adapter could pass the intended collector CI gate.
findings.evidence: Direct inspection of workflow path and pytest selectors.
findings.validation_reason: Literal workflow selectors omit all new collection tests.

findings.title: Catalog resume also trusts cached public repository inventory
findings.suggested_fix: Recheck repository native identity and current public status before catalog content endpoints; record inaccessible without saving private payloads.
findings.first_evidence: The three-request interrupted catalog regression resumes after visibility changes and fetches a private content endpoint.
findings.evidence: The three-request interrupted catalog regression resumes after visibility changes and fetches a private content endpoint.
findings.validation_reason: A targeted PostgreSQL transport-to-writer regression fails before the correction.

findings.title: Authenticated drafts enter public release evidence
findings.suggested_fix: Remove draft/unpublished releases from both observation payloads and persisted page envelopes, retaining raw response/item budget counts.
findings.first_evidence: A response containing two published releases and one draft saves all three observations plus the unpublished sentinel in page evidence.
findings.evidence: A response containing two published releases and one draft saves all three observations plus the unpublished sentinel in page evidence.
findings.validation_reason: A targeted PostgreSQL transport-to-writer regression fails before the correction.
